content: Es llamativo leer hoy a tantos en Estados Unidos, y también en el resto de América, repetir el escándalo que vocaliza Donald Trump frente a la presentación de Bad Bunny en el #SuperBowlLX. No sorprende demasiado que esa reacción se reproduzca en los mismos espacios que respaldan a Javier Milei, Jair Bolsonaro, José Antonio Kast o Álvaro Uribe. Más que una discusión estética, lo que se activa es un sistema de afinidades ideológicas que atraviesa fronteras y contextos. La reacción no se ordena alrededor del gusto ni de la música, sino de un conjunto de valores, dogmas y jerarquías culturales que se sienten interpelados cuando el centro deja de responder a lo esperado. El conflicto opera en un plano más profundo, ligado a la forma en que se concibe quién puede ocupar la escena y bajo qué condiciones. Al mismo tiempo, ese escándalo no apareció con la misma intensidad frente a figuras como Sean Combs (P. Diddy) o Harvey Weinstein, ni frente a los circuitos de poder, dinero y celebridades que durante años habilitaron, encubrieron o naturalizaron abusos de todo tipo mientras modelaban una lectura del mundo funcional a ese mismo entramado. La indignación no se activó ahí. Operó de manera selectiva. Resulta todavía más elocuente observar quiénes concentran hoy su energía en cuestionar la performance de Benito. Son los mismos espacios que celebraron operaciones de fuerza del poder estadounidense en nombre de intereses estratégicos, incluso cuando esas acciones implicaron violaciones abiertas al derecho internacional. No hubo ahí escándalo moral ni alarma republicana. Tampoco aparece una condena consistente frente al accionar del ICE, aun cuando sus prácticas derivan en detenciones arbitrarias, persecuciones cotidianas y episodios de violencia que alcanzan a ciudadanos estadounidenses, familias enteras y niños muy pequeños cuyo único rasgo común es el origen latino o la condición migrante. Esa violencia no genera tapas ni debates encendidos. Pasa como fondo. En esos sectores que hoy se apuran en decir “odio a Bad Bunny”, “a mí no me representa”, predominó durante años el silencio. No fue neutralidad sino una forma de complicidad social sostenida por una incomodidad cuidadosamente administrada. La indignación funciona así como una aduana cultural. Se activa para controlar gestos simbólicos mientras deja pasar intactas a las estructuras que sostuvieron abusos reales. Al artista se le reclama una pureza moral que nunca se exigió a los espacios de poder que produjeron y protegieron esas violencias. Para los sectores conservadores la cultura no funciona como un adorno sino como un espacio donde se naturalizan posiciones, gestos y expectativas. Ahí se aprende a ocupar un lugar y a reconocer la escena como propia. Ese aprendizaje circula sin necesidad de ser nombrado. Se vuelve hábito, clima, repetición. La perturbación aparece cuando esa escena deja de responder a lo previsto. No llega ordenada ni busca explicarse. Se manifiesta como ruido, como una reacción anterior a cualquier elaboración posterior, acompañada por la sensación persistente de que algo se desplazó sin autorización. En ese marco surgen comparaciones forzadas, incluso con figuras como Jeffrey Epstein. Sus crímenes no están en discusión. Lo que resulta llamativo es el uso que se hace de ese dato, arrastrado hacia asociaciones que no buscan esclarecer nada. Un gesto artístico queda sometido a una lógica de condena equivalente a la de una trama criminal. El efecto es ruido. Un ruido que licúa responsabilidades concretas y, al mismo tiempo, permite recomponer jerarquías culturales por acumulación y no por sentido. Las músicas ligadas a experiencias sociales concretas arrastran una historia extensa de descalificación asociada al orden. En torno a ellas se aprendió a fijar bordes, a decidir hasta dónde podía llegar una voz. Lo que aparece no es una novedad súbita sino una presencia sostenida. El cuerpo permanece. La escena queda atravesada por esa presencia.

Just before it, she got her 4th cancer diagnosis. Over 15 years ago: stage 3C breast cancer. We didn’t know how long she’d have. Chemo, radiation—she kicked its ass. Years later: lung spot, major surgery to remove part of her lung. Battling skin cancer ongoing. Now: NET on her liver, possibly thyroid too. content: Hoping all my new Patriots followers see this—please share and send positive vibes to my mom. ❤️ I've been hesitant to post this the past month, but with the Super Bowl tomorrow, I don't care anymore. In December, my mom and I went to the @Patriots vs @Ravens game. I live in Maryland, she’s in PA, so games together have been rare—but this one was unforgettable. Just before it, she got her 4th cancer diagnosis. Over 15 years ago: stage 3C breast cancer. We didn’t know how long she’d have. Chemo, radiation—she kicked its ass. Years later: lung spot, major surgery to remove part of her lung. Battling skin cancer ongoing. Now: NET on her liver, possibly thyroid too. The deeper I research, the harder it hits—rare, scary terms, endless Google spirals. But the Patriots have always been our distraction, our joy, our good memories. This year especially. Before the Ravens game, I reached out to both teams for anything to lift her spirits. Tommy from the Patriots contacted me—turns out the @Ravens saw my message first and passed it along. Hate to say it, but massive shahtaht to the Ravens organization for that. Gained huge respect for them. At the game, Tommy met us at our seats and surprised her with a signed @chrisgonzo28 jersey! She’s taken me to so many games growing up—to flip that and surprise her was incredibly fulfilling. Win or lose tomorrow, watching another Pats Super Bowl with her (from different states this time) is gonna hit hard emotionally. She’s been open that she’s afraid this could be her last. As a dad now to two kids watching their first Pats Super Bowl, it all feels so full-circle. That Gonzo jersey has been set up in her pub (yep, she has her own pub 🍻) for every game since that chilly night in Baltimore—and it hasn’t let us down yet! Hoping it brings a little more magic tomorrow on the #StairwayToSeven. Let’s go Pats! For my mom. 💙🏈 #NEPats #FuckCancer #SuperBowlLX

content: Last night I didn’t watch the #SuperBowl in person. I wasn’t in a stadium or surrounded by thousands of people. I watched the halftime show quietly from my office near my home. Just me, a screen, and a moment I didn’t expect to feel so deeply. And I’m really glad I did. What @sanbenito delivered wasn’t just a performance – it was a reminder. A reminder of who we are. Of where we come from. Of how powerful culture, language, and pride truly are. He stood on one of the biggest stages in the world and sang every word in Spanish without apology. He celebrated roots, history, and identity in a way that felt fearless and honest. And when he named all of those countries – Chile, Argentina, Mexico, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, and so many more – it felt personal. It felt like recognition. Like unity. Like love being spoken out loud. The quote that stayed with me the most was simple and perfect: “The only thing more powerful than hate is love.” That line hit hard. Because I know what it means to keep going when life tests you. I know what it feels like to be overlooked, misunderstood, or counted out. My whole journey has been built on resilience, strength, and perseverance. 🙏🏽 And seeing someone stand proudly in their truth on a global stage reminded me why those things matter. Love over hate. Pride over fear. Unity over division. That performance wasn’t political to me – it was human. It was hopeful. It was proof that no matter what language we speak or what flag we come from, we all want to be seen and respected. Moments like that matter. Representation matters. Culture matters. 🎙️ And last night, from a small office near my house, I felt proud. Proud of my heritage, proud of our diversity, and proud to live in a world where love can still be louder than anything else. That’s the America I believe in! ♥️🗽🇺🇸🇩🇴 #BenitoBowl #halftimeshow #superbowlLX #superbowl2026

content: If you’ve followed me for a bit you know I suffer from parosmia, and it sucks. Five years in and slowly healing, some days are better than others, but I still miss the game day treats. I still prepare for others, but, for me…I just can’t. Playing around this morning cause I miss pico (salsa is cooked, pico is raw) so much it hurts. I can eat tomatoes, but that’s about it for pico. Today I diced some celery, another thing I can eat without repercussions added to diced tomatoes, kosher salt and found this amazing spice blend which I can tolerate. Cant really taste the flavors, but get a bit of heat, which is a good thing. Tomatoes ✔️ Celery ✔️ Kosher Salt ✔️ SnS Triple S Blend ✔️ (Garlic, Onion, Gluten & MSG Free) White Corn Tortilla Chips It’s been a couple hours since I enjoyed the texture of chilled tomatoes, crunchy celery (mimicked onion) and as of yet, still no issues. Chaque geste artistique devient un outil de liberté et de reconnaissance. 🏈 Et sur le terrain, les Seahawks de Seattle ont dominé les Patriots 29‑13. content: Super Bowl LXI: Seahawks set as early favorite in 2027. Super Bowl LXI in the Los Angeles area falls on Valentine’s Day next year, and 31 teams will again be going home with heartbreak. With a little more than a year to go, sportsbooks are still feeling a lot of love for the NFC West. The Seattle Seahawks are favored on consensus odds for Super Bowl LXI to again represent the NFC by a slim margin at +750 over the Los Angeles Rams (+800). The Buffalo Bills (+1000) have the best odds on the AFC side. The Rams would be playing at their home field, SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif., where they won Super Bowl LVI, if they can overcome the Seahawks and the rest of the NFC to get back to the big game. Seattle eliminated Los Angeles in the NFC title game 31-27. Buffalo’s biggest competition comes from the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots, as well as the Baltimore Ravens (+1200). The Ravens made a coaching change after missing the playoffs in an attempt to catch lightning in a bottle as the Patriots did by hiring Mike Vrabel following consecutive 4-13 seasons. The Green Bay Packers (+1300) are followed by the Los Angeles Chargers, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions and Kansas City Chiefs on the next rung at +1500. The Lions and Chiefs missed the playoffs but still have the core pieces and foundational players from recent runs of success. A big question for the Chiefs is Patrick Mahomes’ recovery from a torn ACL. Four 2025 playoff teams — the San Francisco 49ers, Denver Broncos, Jacksonvulle Jaguars and Houston Texans — are all +2000 to win the Lombari Trophy in 2027. On the other end of the spectrum, the New York Jets have the longest odds to win the Super Bowl at 250-1 or plus +25000. hey are below the Miami Dolphins (225-1), Arizona Cardinals (200-1), New Orleans Saints (175-1), Carolina Panthers (150-1) and Tennessee Titans (150-1). content: 🏈 Would America’s most beloved game even exist without Theodore Roosevelt? As you watch Super Bowl LX, you’re witnessing a game that nearly disappeared forever. In 1905, football was brutal. No helmets. No forward pass. Formations like the “flying wedge” left dozens dead and hundreds injured each season. Critics called it a “death harvest.” Schools like Columbia and Stanford dropped the sport entirely. Enter President Theodore Roosevelt. A fan of “manly sport” but not of fatal violence, Roosevelt summoned college leaders to the White House. He demanded reform — or else football would be banned nationwide. His influence led to sweeping changes: •The forward pass was legalized •Dangerous mass plays were banned •A new governing body emerged: today’s NCAA These reforms didn’t just save football — they reshaped it. Roosevelt turned a deadly brawl into the foundation of the fast-paced, high-drama game we love today. So when you see a deep touchdown pass or a clean hit on Super Bowl Sunday, tip your cap to Teddy. Without him, there might be no football at all. 🏟️🇺🇸 #SuperBowlLX #FootballHistory #TeddyRoosevelt #GridironGlory #NFL #HistoryOfFootball #SuperBowlSunday #ThankTeddy

content: نعم، صحيح أن الذئب يُعتبر حيواناً مفترساً، لكنه في ذات الوقت يتمتع بغريزة أمومة قوية تجاه صغاره. غريزة الأمومة هي شعور عميق في الكائنات الحية، يشمل الرغبة في حماية ورعاية الأبناء، وهذا ينطبق أيضاً على الذئاب. الذئب الأم، عند ولادة صغارها، تكرس الكثير من الجهد والاهتمام في تربيتهم. تبني عائلة الذئب حياة اجتماعية معقدة، حيث تتشارك الأدوار بين الذكور والإناث في الاعتناء بالصغار. الذئبة تقوم بإرضاعهم وحمايتهم من المخاطر، بينما يساعدها الذئب الآخر في الإتيان بالطعام وتوفير الحماية. طوال فترة نمو الصغار، تقوم الذئاب بأمور عدة تضمن بقاءهم ونموهم بشكل صحي. يعتمد الصغار على أسرهم أولاً، حيث تتعلم منهم كيفية الصيد والبقاء بأمان في البرية. غريزة الأمومة لدى الذئاب تعكس الطبيعة الاجتماعية لهذه الحيوانات، حيث تعتمد البقاء على العمل الجماعي والتعاون العائلي. إن العلاقة بين الذئب الأم وصغارها تُظهر جانباً مهماً من الحياة البرية، مما يدل على أن الغرائز ليست فقط استجابة للبقاء، بل تشمل أيضاً مشاعر الحب والرعاية التي تربط الأمهات بأبنائهن. في النهاية، برغم كون الذئاب مفترسة، إلا أن غريزة الأمومة التي تظهرها تساعد في الحفاظ على سلالة الذئاب وتعزز الروابط الاجتماعية التي تضمن استمرارية حياتهم في بيئتهم. #BBMzansiS6 #SuperBowlLX #uzaksehir

Frente a un mensaje político previo de Donald Trump, Bad Bunny respondió con arte: cantó desde las gradas entre la gente, vistió la bandera de Puerto Rico e interpeló al público en español. Offensive Struggles for New England: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye faced relentless pressure, suffering two sacks in the first quarter alone. Most of this pressure originated from the left side of the line against rookie starters. Missed Opportunities: Seattle missed a chance to extend their lead when Sam Darnold overthrew a wide-open Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a potential long touchdown play on their second possession. La respuesta política no tardó. Donald Trump calificó el espectáculo como “terrible” y “una bofetada” al país, criticó el idioma, el baile y hasta la nueva regla de kickoff de la NFL, y remató con su consigna “MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN”. En el escenario más grande del mundo, frente a millones de espectadores, Green Day no solo tocó; lanzó una declaración política que ya está rompiendo el internet. Lo que muchos esperaban como un show de nostalgia pop-punk, se convirtió en el acto más anti-establishment jamás visto en un Super Bowl. La banda liderada por Billie Joe Armstrong hizo retumbar las paredes del estadio con "American Idiot", el himno que nació como una crítica feroz a la política estadounidense y que hoy, en plena cadena nacional, sonó más vigente (y agresivo) que nunca. Los puntos clave de la noche: Letra sin censura: La banda no se guardó nada, adaptando versos que muchos interpretaron como un dardo directo hacia el clima político actual y el legado de figuras como Donald Trump. Transmisión global: Un mensaje de rebeldía pura proyectado en el evento que es, por excelencia, el símbolo del capitalismo y el patriotismo estadounidense. Redes sociales en llamas: Mientras unos celebran el "regreso del punk con causa", otros cuestionan si el Super Bowl es el lugar para este tipo de mensajes. ¿Es este el momento más "anti-gringo" en la historia del deporte de EE. UU. o simplemente rock n' roll en su estado más puro? Lo cierto es que, después de esto, el Super Bowl no volverá a sentirse igual. 🏟️🇺🇸 ¿Qué te pareció el show? ¿Valentía pura o fuera de lugar? content: How Will AI Impact the Future of Football? Will robots replace humans on the field? Could the NFL become the RFL? And will the Super Bowl become the Ultra Bowl? This sci-fi author has some answers. Watching AI and robotics increasingly shape our economy and society, I’m amazed that a sci-fi scenario I imagined about the future of football in my 2014 novel ULTRA BOWL seems more and more probable. A plausible argument can be made that concerns about football’s health hazards, combined with our economy’s increasing reliance on technology, robotics, and artificial intelligence, will result in profound changes to the game that has been called America’s “secular religion.” If there’s a Super Bowl C (100), there’s a good chance it’ll be played by robots. Hear me out… Robot football is a logical extension of many of today’s trends in our increasingly AI-enabled world. Robots drive our cars, fly our planes, and grow our food. What won’t they be doing 10, 20, 50 years from now? Technology has allowed us to outsource many aspects of our lives. AI increasingly does our thinking, Google our remembering, Facebook, Instagram and X our socializing, and drones our fighting. Eventually, we may outsource the violence in football to robots. Here’s a scenario that could play out over the next fifty years. Fantasy? Possibility? You be the judge. Football: The Next Fifty Years? China, the manufacturing center of the world, increasingly employs robots. During an International Robotics Exhibition a decade from now, China unveils a robot football team. What better way to challenge America culturally and technologically than by announcing a series of robot football exhibition games with Japan. The media cynically labels these robot games the ultimate version of “kick the can.” But year after year, robot performances improve and a robot football league, the RFL, is born. What began for many as a joke, soon becomes a worldwide phenomenon with legions of hardcore fans. And it isn’t long before the NFL is besieged by a public clamoring for a “friendly” exhibition game with the RFL, which the NFL declines. As the world economy increasingly depends on AI and robotics, Corporate America realizes that robot football is the perfect marketing vehicle. If the Super Bowl is the most prized and viewed ad space, an actual game of robots, showcasing the latest AI technology, is one mega ad. The game’s point-spread will determine tech supremacy and ultimately market share. Fearing America could lose the world robotics market, the tech industry lobbies the government to develop a U.S. robot football team to compete in the RFL. By mid-century, the U. S. government decides to establishes NAFA — the National Android Football Administration. Like the old NASA, its mission isn’t to put a man on the moon, but to field the best robot football team in the world. At first, the U.S. team is no match for the other nations of the RFL. Each year, however, NAFA unveils improved models that incorporate the latest advances in AI technology, and America quickly becomes competitive. As the audience for robot football grows, interest in NFL football declines. To compete with the increasingly popular RFL, the NFL waives the rules that protect players in order to make the game more “entertaining.” Despite this “blood & guts” strategy, NFL attendance continues to drop. Eventually, the interests of a growing segment of Main Street, for whom football is too dangerous, and the interests of Wall Street combine in a powerful political movement that legislates the abolition of professional football. The NFL is disbanded. The prohibition of football, admittedly an overreaction, lasts less than a decade. By the time it’s repealed, it’s too late — humans have stopped playing football. It’s only a matter of time before the RFL becomes the ultimate technological battleground between nations. The championship game is called the Ultra Bowl because if a nation stumbles, stocks tumble and economies crumble. In only a few decades, the Ultra Bowl evolves from a freak sideshow spectacle to the preeminent global event that determines world economic power. Fantasy today. Reality tomorrow? The idea of robots playing football sounds crazy, I know. But many of the things we take for granted today sounded crazy only a few decades ago. In Two Minute Warning: How Concussion, Crime, and Controversy Could Kill the NFL, veteran sports journalist Mike Freeman ends his book by introducing my sci-fi novel ULTRA BOWL. After quoting me at length about the very real possibility of robot football in the future, he concludes, “I’m not laughing.” So next time you see the Fox Sports’ NFL mascot Cleatus the Robot, ask yourself: Is it a harbinger of things to come? It’s hard to imagine our NFL “gladiators” not going head-to-head on any given future Sunday, but 2,000 years ago, the mighty Romans believed that their gladiators would still be “fighting to the death” today. Why, you might ask, should the speculations of a sci-fi author be taken seriously? Since the late 19th century, when Jules Verne wrote about submarines in 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea, writers have tried to imagine what tomorrow might look like. In many cases, they were right: space travel, credit cards, radar, solar power, voicemail, flat-screen TVs, virtual reality, and even atomic bombs were first imagined by science fiction writers. Who knows, I may be one of them. ___________ #football #SuperBowl #SuperBowlLX #ArtificialIntelligence #Robots #book

When a nationally recognized comedian such as Jimmy Kimmel is subjected to organized advertiser pressure and institutional backlash following political expression, and when a political activist such as Charlie Kirk faces coordinated deplatforming, event cancellation, and exclusion campaigns for dissenting views, the machinery reveals itself plainly: speech is tolerated only by alignment, not by principle. A Republic cannot endure where tongues bow while spirits do not. Our elder citizens — those who have looked directly into the eyes of history - recognize this pattern. They recall the narrowing of narratives in Europe before the Second World War, the manipulation of mass media, the illusion of choice amid orchestrated distraction. Tyranny rarely arrives by decree; it is normalized, entertained, and excused until resistance becomes unthinkable. The controlled flow of information — news that shows only what the powerful permit, narratives that distract from corruption, endless noise drowning out truth - is no accident. It is machinery. Its purpose is not enlightenment, but pacification. Suffering has not vanished; it has been relocated beyond the lens. Wealth accumulates in towers while the foundations beneath them crack. There exists no vast national refuge for the homeless, no great campaign to restore dignity to the forgotten. Veterans sleep beneath bridges; children know hunger more intimately than hope; families wander between shelter and despair. Government persists in ritual while forgetting the oldest truth of self-rule: without the people it has no power - and without consent it ceases to exist. Across American cities, public space itself has been altered to prevent rest and to criminalize visibility. Metal spikes are embedded beneath overpasses; concrete benches are segmented with armrests placed inches apart; sidewalks are grooved, angled, or studded to cause pain when lying down; flat surfaces are broken by raised dividers; ledges are armored to repel the human body. These are not accidents of design. They are policies rendered in steel and stone, choosing displacement over shelter and banishment over care. Most grievous still are judicial decisions permitting racial profiling by immigration enforcers — a poisonous contradiction against the Constitution's promise of equal protection. To target a citizen or immigrant by appearance alone is to resurrect the ghosts of injustices the nation once vowed to bury. Within immigration enforcement and detention, the distance between law and cruelty has narrowed dangerously. Federal agencies have expanded recruitment through public advertisements, calling upon ordinary citizens to enlist, offering bonuses, benefits, and expedited hiring, rapidly vesting extraordinary power in individuals with limited training or oversight. Documented reporting, sworn testimony, and litigation describe people beaten, dragged, and thrown to the ground during enforcement actions, sustaining broken bones, head trauma, internal injuries, and lasting harm. Inside detention facilities, credible accounts detail medical neglect, sexual assault, psychological abuse, and deaths later obscured by administrative language. When force becomes procedural, law ceases to restrain power - it authorizes it. A nation may enforce its borders without surrendering its conscience. If a society permits the normalization of violence against any group — legal or illegal, citizen or foreigner - it teaches the world that human dignity is conditional. And once dignity is conditional, no border, no ocean, no alliance can insulate the world from the instability that follows. Foreign nations - unbound by our domestic politics - look upon America with troubled eyes.

content: @USAstandstrong @simonateba The halftime show celebrates roots that are 100% part of USA culture too. Puerto Rico’s been a U.S. territory since 1898. All of its citizens born there have been full U.S. citizens since the Jones Act of 1917. This means Puerto Rican culture is inherently woven into the American tapestry—think of it as a distinct thread in the multicultural U.S. fabric, similar to how Hawaiian or Native American traditions are. Their citizens have served in the U.S. military (nearly 20,000 in WWI alone). That said, identities can be complex—many Puerto Ricans proudly identify as both Boricua and American, while emphasizing their unique Hispanic roots over full assimilation. ￼￼ ￼ Politically, Puerto Rico isn’t a state (it’s an unincorporated territory with limited federal voting rights), so some folks debate how “American” it feels culturally. ￼ ￼ But legally and historically, it’s undeniably part of the USA, and events like this halftime show highlight how Puerto Rican culture explodes onto the national stage. content: It's gonna be another #SuperBowl final tonight. Somehow somehow now, late Herbert Wigwe is the first person that comes to my mind anytime the word superbowl final comes up. Today makes it two years since that ill-fated helicopter crash that claimed the lives of Wigwe family and a few others. May their souls continue to rest in peace. Anyways, life goes on! I have seen superbowl final for four straight years now but I am still not a fan of American football. I don't think watching only one game in a year is enough to make me a fan of a sport. I don't have any favorite between the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots who are the two finalists this year. I will just wish them both best of luck, and hope that the best team win. I also hope that the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) rumoured sting operation won't make a mess of this year's final as there are lots of ongoing rumours that ICE agents will be storming Santa Clara in California to arrest dozens of illegal migrants. #SuperBowlLX #SuperBowl2026 #SuperBowlSunday QT @olajideobe: Today is another #SuperBowl final night! I'm not sure yet if I'll be up till late in the night to watch this year's final. However, this #SuperBowl comes with mixed feelings for me because it was about this time last year that Herbert Wigwe, the late MD/CEO of Access Bank, died in a tragic chopper crash while he was on his way to watch the superbowl final. He died in company of his wife, first son and four other people. May God grant their souls an eternal rest. In another twist of event, Donald Trump will become the first ever sitting president to attend the Super Bowl. Like him or loathe him, Trump is fast becoming the most revolutionary leader in modern times since after Abraham Lincoln. In his first three weeks since his return to the Oval Office ss the 47th president of the United States of America, he has already signed more than 50 executive orders. Trump says things others refuse to say and sees what others refuse to see. I sincerely wish Trump succeeds, because his success is a win for the rest of the world too, albeit his most vociferous mantra is "Make America Great Again" (MAGA). Tonight's final will be a repeat of 2023 final as the Chiefs will square it out against the Philly Eagles. Will the Chiefs, the defending champion, make it a 3peat of victories or will the Eagles get their revenge for the 2023 defeat at the hands of the Chiefs? I am not a fan of American football per say, and I don't care which side emerges victorious tonight. Nonetheless, I wish both Kansas City Chiefs and the Philadelphia Eagles best of luck and a successful outing at the #SuperBowlLIX. Let the best team win. #SuperBowl2025

content: The Washington Post has once again graced us with the journalistic equivalent of showing up to a birthday party with a PowerPoint about your ex's unresolved trauma. Behold their masterpiece: "What do we make of Colin Kaepernick now?"—because nothing screams "Super Bowl Sunday vibes" like dusting off a nine-year-old protest controversy while Seahawks fans are busy painting their faces blue and Patriots fans are calculating how many more rings Brady would have if he hadn't retired twice. In a stroke of pure genius, @washingtonpost decided the defining storyline for @Patriots vs. @Seahawks at Levi's Stadium isn't the actual game, the underdog narratives, Bad Bunny's halftime show, or even whether the field will survive another earthquake scare. No, it's time to solemnly ponder Kaepernick's legacy—right now, during the one day a year when 100 million Americans explicitly tune in to not ponder anything deeper than whether the next commercial will make them cry or buy a truck. The stadium hosted him once? Check. Society still has problems? Double check. Therefore: mandatory thinkpiece injection. Never mind that Kap hasn't thrown a meaningful pass since the Obama administration or that most viewers just want to see if Belichick's ghost is still haunting Foxboro. This is peak "we're very serious people" energy from an outlet that recently laid off half its sports desk but somehow found the bandwidth to re-litigate 2016 kneeling ethics. In a world crying out for more hot takes about football games actually involving football, WaPo bravely asks the question no one asked: "Hey, remember that guy? Let's make him the main character again while everyone else is eating wings." The real question WaPo people should be asking, but are incapable of asking, is "What can I do to make this a better, profitable product?" #SuperBowlLX #SuperBowl @washingtonpost QT @washingtonpost: The Super Bowl is being played in Colin Kaepernick's former home stadium, at a societal moment that echoes the issues he forced football fans to confront nearly 10 years ago, after he kneeled during the national anthem before a 49ers game. https://t.co/TX2l7r7msx

The whole field became ‘La Casita’: sugarcane fields, a taco stand, a vintage truck, dancers everywhere, even a wedding happening on the grass. He opened with ‘titi me pregunto’, went through MONACO, Yo Perreo Sola (on top of the actual pink casita!), and dropped the message on the jumbotron: ‘The only thing more powerful than hate is love.’ Then he handed his Album of the Year Grammy to a little kid watching at home on TV. Pure chills.Surprise guests? Lady Gaga came out in a baby-blue gown for ‘Die With a Smile’, Ricky Martin hit the stage for ‘LO QUE LE PASÓ A HAWAii’, and the casita was PACKED with Pedro Pascal, Cardi B, Karol G, Jessica Alba, Alix Earle, Young Miko — all dancing like it was a block party in San Juan.And while the world was losing it over Benito… Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton made their first high-profile public appearance together in a suite, laughing, chatting, looking cozy AF. The timeline is still recovering.This wasn’t just a halftime show. It was a cultural moment, a love letter to the diaspora, and low-key the soft launch of the year.Still buzzing. sam darnold won people's hearts Who had the best moment for you? #SuperBowlLX #BadBunny

content: Un DATO que sorprende a casi todo el mundo sobre el Super Bowl 🏈: Los artistas que se presentan en el halftime show (el show de medio tiempo) prácticamente NO ganan dinero directo por actuar. La NFL no les paga un caché o fee de presentación como lo harían en un concierto normal. En cambio: • Solo reciben el pago mínimo por escala sindical (union scale) obligatorio por ley laboral (a través de SAG-AFTRA u otros sindicatos). Esto suele ser alrededor de $1,000 dólares por día (algunos reportes hablan de $671 por la actuación + unos $1,800 por ensayos en total, o hasta $1,246/día según contratos recientes de 2025). • Es decir, un artista como #BadBunny (quien está headlining el Super Bowl LX de 2026), Kendrick Lamar (2025), Usher, Rihanna o Beyoncé… se lleva literalmente unos pocos miles de dólares en total por todo el trabajo (ensayos + show). ¿Por qué aceptan? Porque la NFL cubre TODOS los gastos de producción (que pueden superar los $10–15 millones por show: escenario, luces, efectos, bailarines, etc.), más viajes, hospedaje y logística para el artista y su equipo. Y lo más importante: la exposición global es brutal. Ejemplos reales del “verdadero pago”: • Un boost masivo en streams y ventas (Kendrick Lamar subió +430% en Spotify post-2025). • Aumento en valor de marca, giras futuras y patrocinios (se estima que Bad Bunny podría generar millones extras en la semana siguiente solo por el streaming y publicidad indirecta). En resumen: ganan casi $0 en salario directo, pero es una de las mejores “inversiones” de marketing que un artista puede tener en su carrera. ¡El show les cuesta poco (o nada) y les genera muchísimo! #SuperBowlLX #SuperBowl60 #NFL #PatriotsVsSeahawks 🏟️
